subject: VelocityX: Customer-led stress run — SLO alignment & k6 logistics
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Lucia Gomez <lucia.gomez@velocityx.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: VelocityX: Customer-led stress run — SLO alignment & k6 logistics

Hi Lucia — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can ensure the upcoming customer-led run validates the right SLOs and keeps your app stable:

Summary of objectives
- Primary SLOs: p95 latency < 250ms (in-region), p99 < 600ms for non-streaming; streaming tail latency target: 95% of chunks < 120ms
- Throughput target: sustained 200 req/s with bursts to 400 req/s for short windows
- Concurrency target: simulate ~500 concurrent sessions with a mix of short/long-lived streaming connections

What we need from VelocityX before the run
- Confirm preferred test window (we suggested Oct 12–13 but flexible)
- Confirm whether your team will execute the k6 script or if you want Redwood to trigger from a customer-facing runbook
- Provide public IPs to add to our allowlist (IPv4 ranges)
- Any firewall rules or proxy headers we should be aware of

What Redwood will provide
- A staging test account + ephemeral API key scoped to the test model and limited token budget (see attachment: redwood-ephemeral-creds.pdf)
- A starter k6 script tuned for streaming and ramp shape (vx-k6-customer-script.js) in Drive (link below)
- On-call SRE and sales engineer (Rishi) to monitor metrics and open a rollback channel

Proposed next steps
1) You confirm the window and who will run the script (VelocityX or Redwood)
2) VelocityX posts the allowlist IPs and any special headers
3) We exchange the test account creds via secure link and schedule a 30-min preflight on the day before the run

Thanks — I’ll loop in Rishi and Monica internally to assign tasks once we have a firm date.

—Neha Kapoor
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: vx-k6-customer-script.js (starter), runbook-stress-template.md

From: Lucia Gomez <lucia.gomez@velocityx.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Tran <alex.tran@vx-consulting.io>, perf@velocityx.com
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: VelocityX: Customer-led stress run — SLO alignment & k6 logistics

Hi Neha — thanks for the clear recap. We’re happy to run the k6 workload from our infra (we want to exercise our egress path). A few clarifying items:

- Window: Oct 12 (US business hours) with an overflow day on Oct 13 if we see any normalization issues
- We will start with the starter script you attached and iterate on ramp shape; Alex (cc’d) will own script edits
- Allowlist IPs (egress from our k6 runners): 34.201.12.0/24, 3.129.45.128/26, 52.14.200.0/22
- For streaming tests: we will open ~200 long-lived chunked connections that push punctuated input every 3–6s to simulate live feeds
- We need a staging API key and endpoint URL with streaming enabled — please confirm token TTL and any per-key rate limits

We’re aiming to validate latency under sustained load and to confirm no request throttling or connection resets when streaming is active.

Lucia
Director of Engineering, VelocityX
lucia.gomez@velocityx.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: VelocityX: Customer-led stress run — SLO alignment & k6 logistics

Rishi/Monica — forwarding Lucia’s confirmation. Action items and owners below (let’s treat this as the run playbook draft):

Action items (owner)
- Add VelocityX egress CIDRs to staging allowlist and validate connectivity (Rishi)
- Generate ephemeral staging API key scoped to model: "redwood-staging-v1" with TTL 48h and token rate limit 1k/min (Monica)
- Prepare a short preflight checklist and monitoring dashboard (Monica)
- Setup Slack channel #vx-loadtest and invite VelocityX and on-call SRE (Neha)

Notes:
- Monica: please attach the ephemeral creds deliverable as a password-protected PDF and include the exact endpoint URL (streaming ws/http chunk URL).
- Rishi: plan to run health-check probes and have a quick rollback plan (drop connection limits / switch to a smaller model) if we hit tail-error rates > 2% for 5m

I’ll propose a short 30-min preflight for Oct 11 to validate connectivity and the script. If you need to change owners let me know.

—Neha

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: VelocityX: Customer-led stress run — SLO alignment & k6 logistics

Adding details from my side:

Ephemeral creds
- File: redwood-ephemeral-creds.pdf (password-protected)
- API key: redwood-stg-vx-xxxxx (will be sent via secure link 24h before run)
- TTL: 48 hours; quota: 2M tokens; rate cap: 1000 req/min

Endpoint details
- HTTP chunked streaming URL: https://staging-api.redwood.com/v1/stream/redwood-staging-v1
- WebSocket URL (alternative): wss://staging-ws.redwood.com/stream/redwood-staging-v1
- Note: chunk latency may be impacted by client batch size; we recommend sending 1–3 tokens per punctuated event for the most realistic simulation

Starter k6 script and ramp suggestion (Drive link)
- Script: vx-k6-customer-script.js (attached) — exercises both short sync requests and long-lived chunked streams, toggles between burst and sustained phases
- Ramp: 10m warmup -> 60m sustained at 200 req/s -> 10m spike to 400 req/s -> 30m cooldown
- Streaming mix: target ~200 concurrent streaming sessions during sustained phase with 20% of sessions sending longer inputs intermittently

Monitoring / dashboards
- I’ll push a temporary Grafana dashboard and CloudWatch alarms tied to p95/p99 latency, stream chunk latency histogram, and error-rate per-minute. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-redwood/vx-k6-scripts

Attachments: redwood-ephemeral-creds.pdf (will be generated), runbook-stress-template.md, vx-k6-customer-script.js

—Monica
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

From: Lucia Gomez <lucia.gomez@velocityx.com>

Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 16:27:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: VelocityX: Customer-led stress run — SLO alignment & k6 logistics

Thanks team — confirmed for Oct 12 with Oct 13 as overflow. We accept the proposed ramp and streaming mix. A couple final asks before preflight:

1) Please add these additional egress CIDRs we discovered in staging: 18.205.45.0/24
2) Can you confirm whether per-key rate limits will trigger a 429 or queueing behavior? We prefer explicit 429s so we can measure throttling behavior during the test
3) Please share the preflight invite (Oct 11) and the Slack channel — Alex (vx-consultant) will join the preflight to help tune the script

We’ll share a short post-run summary and the raw k6 metrics; if there’s anything else you need ahead of the preflight, ping me.

—Lucia

Attachments: none
